name: rv220w-openwrt-promotion-toolkit
safety_policy: RAM-only validation; no automated flash writes
platform_integration: Cisco RV220W hardware-proven RAM-validation DTB profile v1.3.2
baseline_status: v1.9.0 hardware validated by complete TFTP RAM boot with all five RJ45 ports operational; no LuCI, WLAN, or persistent flash attempt
key_change: run9 VLAN proof promoted into B53 CPU-port initialization patch 998; rj45-full is now hardware-proven for complete RAM boot and five-port wired operation

candidate.derivation: all non-DTB file-backed sections from proven v1.3.1; exact v1.3.0 nor@0,0 child restored; 400 MHz UART retained

discovery_profile.switch_binding: disabled; no B53 child in DT
discovery_profile.policy: passive discovery; direct Clause 22 reads plus selector-only pseudo-PHY writes to 0x1e registers 0x10/0x11; no switch data writes, reset, DSA binding, or flash writes

port_mapping.status: hardware validated passive topology plus LAN DSA runs 1-5
port_mapping.eth2: no observed link or traffic; strong board-level inference ties it to an unpopulated optional RJ45/magnetics footprint
port_mapping.phy5: present with distinct PHY ID; internal/non-external role not yet assigned
port_mapping.evidence: NONE/WAN UART scans prove PHY0; LAN1-LAN4 scans prove PHY1-PHY4; host counters map WAN to eth1 and LAN aggregate to eth0
port_mapping.switch_port5: hardware-proven 1G full-duplex DSA conduit to Octeon eth1; run9 restores bidirectional WAN forwarding when port5 participates in the selected ordinary VLAN-table domain
port_mapping.switch_port8: hardware-proven DSA conduit to Octeon eth0; all four LAN ports pass 1000/full and full-MTU traffic

current_stage.name: hardware-proven full-RJ45 RAM-boot OpenWrt profile
current_stage.transport: hardware-proven RAM-only TFTP boot through stock U-Boot; no saveenv or flash writes
current_stage.topology: wan/port0 -> CPU port5 -> eth1; lan1-lan4/ports1-4 -> CPU port8 -> eth0 -> br-lan
current_stage.affinity: standard DSA rtnetlink mapping before netifd: wan -> eth1; lan1-lan4 -> eth0; generic B53 conduit callback preserves disjoint PVLAN domains
current_stage.policy: firewall4 separates LAN and WAN; LAN-to-WAN forwarding and masquerading enabled; WAN-to-LAN forwarding rejected; PPP/PPPoE available; no LuCI or flash-write automation
current_stage.timing: port5 and port8 rgmii-rxid, both hardware-proven at 1000/full
current_stage.run9_result: port5 PVID change alone failed; adding port5 to VID0 restored WAN, restoring the original table restored failure, and a separate VID1 {0,5} domain also passed; ordinary VLAN membership/classification is proven causal
current_stage.driver_fix: merge dsa_cpu_ports(ds) into B53 enabled_ports before generic VLAN setup so every firmware-described CPU conduit receives the default PVID and VLAN membership
current_stage.hardware_isolation: PVLAN WAN domain {0,5}; LAN domain {1,2,3,4,8}; Linux bridge contains only lan1-lan4
current_stage.next_after_rj45: preserve final regression logs, evaluate optional LuCI size, promote LEDs/reset/watchdog, investigate WLAN, then design and qualify a recovery-preserving persistent layout
current_stage.hardware_validation: complete boot to running OpenWrt with LAN1-LAN4 and WAN initialized and operational
current_stage.limitations: experimental/unpolished; no LuCI; BCM4322 Wi-Fi not operational; no persistent installation or onboard NOR write attempted

lan_dsa_hardware_validation.errors: no interface errors/drops during test windows; no sustained Octeon receive error 10 after v1.7.6
